cards.title: Neural and Experiential Dynamics of High-Ventilation Breathwork Mirror Psychedelic States
cards.post: Background: While recent studies have begun to pinpoint physiological and neural changes involved in altered states of consciousness (ASCs) evoked by HVB, the interplay between neural and experiential dynamics throughout an HVB session … Methods: Here we tracked neural activity (via 64-channel EEG recordings) as well as subjective experience depth and content in 25 experienced HVB practitioners across resting-state recordings interleaved throughout a naturalistic HVB session. Results: We find that neural dynamics evoked by HVB emulate the most robust neural signatures of classical psychedelic states, specifically (1) loosening of temporal structure, including broadband cortical desynchronization, increased signal complexity, and decreased oscillatory power in the Alpha (8 - 13 Hz) range, and (2) reorganization of spatial structure, including a flattening of cortical processing … Conclusion: Together, these results identify unifying neural features of psychedelic-like ASCs regardless of induction method, demonstrating that cortical states triggered by psychedelics can also be accessed by non-pharmacological routes, and breathwork is a powerful way …

cards.title: Changes in self-related cognitive processes and depressive symptom severity following a single, moderate dose of psilocybin in depressed patients.
cards.venue: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
cards.post: Background: Psychedelic-assisted therapy, particularly with psilocybin, is increasingly proposed as a treatment for major depressive disorder, yet the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying its effects remain under investigation. Methods: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, individuals diagnosed with major depressive disorder received a single, moderate dose of psilocybin (0.215 mg kg-1) or placebo, with the same psychological support. Results: Compared with placebo, the psilocybin group exhibited significant reductions in depressive symptoms and a significant increase in positive self-concept two weeks after substance administration. Changes in self-concept were significantly correlated with decreased depressive scores. Conclusion: These findings extend prior evidence linking psychedelics to changes in self-referential processing and self-concept and demonstrate that such changes occur concurrently with reductions in depressive symptoms.

cards.title: The 5-HT2A receptor inverse agonist/antagonist volinanserin modulates motor outcomes and regulates lateral septum-prefrontal and lateral septum-hippocampal functional connectivity.
cards.post: Background: While there is evidence for efficacy of 5-HT 2A R targeting drugs in schizophrenia and other disorders, the impact of volinanserin on circuit-level brain function and connectivity remains unknown. Methods: Here, we test the impact of volinanserin on behaviours in mice relevant to a range of symptom domains in schizophrenia. Results: In terms of brain activity, volinanserin increased activity in the lateral septum (LS), dorsal raphé and nucleus accumbens, while reducing activity in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). Volinanserin also reduced LS functional connectivity with the PFC, hippocampus and amygdala. Conclusion: These data highlight the LS as a key locus of action for volinanserin's putative antipsychotic effects and support a role for this region in mediating the behavioural impact of 5-HT 2A R targeting drugs.

cards.title: Exploring subacute effects of a DMT and harmine meditation retreat on the brain's control energy landscape
cards.post: Background: Modeling the brain as a controllable structural network allows the estimation of the control energy (CE) required to reach functional states, where low-CE states are more accessible. Methods: This exploratory study uses rs-fMRI from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 39; 19 verum [N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) + harmine, Ayahuasca-inspired formulation], 20 placebo) scanned before and after a three-day meditation retreat. Results: Globally, we found no systematic shift in the distribution of CE between transitions, however mean CE increased in both groups at the long timescale approach. In the short timescale approach, the visual network (VN) showed a FDR-BH CE decrease within the verum group, consistent with reduced dynamical demand in a region acutely engaged by DMT. Conclusion: Overall, the two timescale lenses surface different network effects, that align with cortical timescale hierarchies.

cards.title: Quantitative Analysis of Lysergic Acid Diethylamide: A Ring Study Among Five Swiss Drug Checking Services.
cards.post: Aim: This study presents an interlaboratory ring trial on LSD quantification within the context of drug checking. Methods: Five Swiss DCS laboratories participated, each employing different analytical techniques (HPLC-DAD, GC-MS, and HPLC-MS/MS) and extraction procedures. Three sample types were distributed: two LSD-infused blotters and one methanolic LSD solution. Results: Interlaboratory variability was low, with relative standard deviations of 8%-16.5% and mean accuracy ranging from -5.3% to -13.0%. Variability was higher for the liquid sample. Conclusion: Reliable chemical data is essential for accurate dosing and effective harm reduction.

cards.title: Quality of Life and the Case for Consent-Based Psilocybin Access – Questions on the Regulatory Framework and Cost
cards.post: Background: Legal access to psilocybin almost always requires a medical diagnosis first, usually treatment-resistant depression (TRD) or severe PTSD, as though informed consent alone was not sufficient. Methods: Just as important, the cost of access is not fixed; it reflects the regulatory framework under which psilocybin is provided. Results: No jurisdiction has yet completed medicines authorisation pathway; the furthest-advanced clinical programme, Compass Pathways' COMP360, met its Phase 3 primary endpoint and reported six-month durability data for TRD by July 2026, and its developer has since signalled an annual cost close to that of esketamine nasal spray, USD 50,000–65,000, or roughly USD 17,000–22,000 per dose. Conclusion: A Canadian case illustrates the institutional and regulatory framework dysfunction, a dying man denied psilocybin for existential relief while approved for medical assistance in dying within weeks, before the article closes with policy recommendations …

cards.title: First-in-class -PET radiotracers for GPR39: A platform for noninvasive target engagement imaging in vivo
cards.post: Background: However, the lack of suitable positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracers has limited the in vivo characterization of GPR39. Methods: Quantitative assessment of GPR39 in vivo could improve our understanding of its role in physiology and disease and facilitate the development and evaluation of targeted therapeutics. Results: GPR39 specificity was further validated in GPR39 knockout mice, which showed 76% (p<0.002) and 90% (p<0.0002) reductions in brain uptake by PET imaging and biodistribution, respectively. Moreover, 5xFAD transgenic mice exhibited significantly lower brain uptake by PET imaging (40%, p<0.0002) and biodistribution (77%, p<0.002), indicating sensitivity of [18F]GPR39 2.1 to disease-associated alterations in GPR39. Conclusion: Collectively, these results establish [18F]GPR39 2.1 as a stable, brain-penetrant, and highly specific PET radiotracer for noninvasive imaging of GPR39 in vivo.

cards.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes
cards.post: Background: Early and accurate identification of neurodegenerative disorders has notable implications for treatment and quality of life. Methods: Whereas neuroimaging-based biomarkers can accurately identify neurodegenerative subtypes, EEG represents a low-cost alternative that could expand access to dementia care. Results: Four factors reflecting neurophysiological oscillations (posterior alpha, Rolandic beta, frontotemporal delta-theta and posterior theta-slow alpha) varied significantly across phenotypes, with attenuation of faster and augmentation of slower rhythms most pronounced in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), dysexecutive Alzheimer disease (AD) and posterior cortical atrophy, whereas factors dominated by eye-movement and muscle artifact showed no robust … Conclusion: Thus, data-driven decomposition of clinical EEG separates oscillatory activity from artifact into factors that track metabolic phenotype, regional metabolism and cognition, capturing both overall slowing and phenotype-specific patterns.

cards.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
cards.post: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). cards.title: Paired-Pulse TMS as a Window into Cortical Microcircuits: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Challenges
cards.post: Background: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) generates cortical electrical currents that, when applied to the primary motor cortex, depolarise neurons, producing motor evoked potentials. cards.title: Domain-level symptom improvement after ketamine and TMS-based stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: a post hoc pooled analysis.
cards.post: Background: We examined short-term symptom-domain improvement after ketamine and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in a post hoc pooled analysis of 159 active-treatment participants from three trials. Methods: Participants received a single ketamine infusion (n = 89) or a two-week TMS course (n = 70); nine had recorded bipolar diagnoses. Results: Mean improvement differed across domains within both modalities (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Main-model between-modality mean contrasts did not meet the adjusted threshold (p = 0.063-0.656); the Somatic contrast did so after adjustment for treatment-resistance categories. Conclusion: These findings describe domain-specific improvement under different treatment regimens.

cards.title: Testing the impact of cannabinoid stimulation on fatty acid amide hydrolase binding in the human brain: pilot [11C]CURB PET study
cards.post: Background: Whether repeated exposure to cannabinoid receptor agonists is associated with changes in FAAH levels in the human brain remains unknown. Methods: In this exploratory Phase IV pilot study, ten healthy adults completed two positron emission tomography scans with the FAAH radiotracer [ 11 C]CURB: a baseline scan and a second scan following a 7-day oral … Results: Nabilone produced subjective effects, including increased marijuana-like drug effects ( p = 0.004), reductions in self-reported energy ( p = 0.02) and clear-headedness ( p = 0.01). No detectable mean change in FAAH was observed across brain regions following seven days of nabilone administration ( p = 0.357). Conclusion: These findings provide preliminary evidence regarding FAAH following repeated cannabinoid receptor agonist exposure and require confirmation in larger, controlled studies.

cards.title: 2-AG as a potential biomarker for predicting response to short-term fluoxetine treatment in a mouse model of depression.
cards.post: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a complex psychiatric condition with significant individual and social impact and marked variability in treatment response. Methods: Fluoxetine, one of the most commonly prescribed antidepressants, influences not only serotonergic signaling but also the endocannabinoid system. Results: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analyses of hippocampal and prefrontal cortex samples revealed that behavioral improvement following short-term fluoxetine treatment was accompanied by increased hippocampal 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), along with reduced GABA and glutamate levels in the prefrontal cortex. Conclusion: These findings suggest that increased 2-AG levels may predict early response to fluoxetine.

cards.title: Stress-induced dorsal striatal dopamine release is associated with changes in functional connectivity to the prefrontal cortex in nicotine-dependent individuals-a preliminary report.
cards.post: Background: The neural mechanism linking stress to addiction pathophysiology remains unclear. Methods: Using a within-subject, multimodal design, we collected PET and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) scans in 8 smokers (6 females; mean age: 32 ± 3.6 years). cards.title: Chronic intracranial neural dynamics forecast treatment response and therapeutic engagement during deep brain stimulation for OCD
cards.venue: USC Mark and Mary Stevens Neuroimaging and Informatics Institute
cards.post: Background: Clinical improvement following psychiatric neuromodulation often requires weeks to months, creating prolonged uncertainty during treatment optimization. Methods: We analyzed nearly 120,000 patient-hours of chronic ventral striatal recordings from 24 patients undergoing deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder. Results: Clinical responders exhibited rapid reductions in neural predictability within two weeks of stimulation, months before they achieved clinical response. The magnitude of this early neural change correlated significantly with eventual symptom reduction. Conclusion: Together, these findings establish a framework for leveraging chronic neural sensing to inform therapeutic target engagement and longitudinal monitoring of treatment response.

cards.title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics.
cards.post: Background: A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. Methods: Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). Results: Memory effects are consistently stronger in wakefulness, indicating richer inter-regional dependencies and more integrated dynamics. Conclusion: These findings establish local memory as a dynamical marker of brain state and position the FDTest as a principled tool for probing the hidden structure of neural dynamics.

cards.title: Aperiodic Exponent as an EEG Marker of Interoceptive Attention during Gastric Fullness
cards.post: Background: Gastric interoceptive attention to internal, bodily signals such as hunger, satiety, and fullness are important for regulating feeding behaviors. Methods: Specifically, understanding cortical representations of self-perceived gastric fullness have yet to be studied in humans. Results: Simultaneous measures of the stomach and heart demonstrate increased vagal drive to peripheral organs. We further find that changes in cortical aperiodic exponent patterns are associated with changes in the frequency of gastric oscillations. Conclusion: Overall, this suggests that the EEG aperiodic exponent may be a useful noninvasive biomarker for assessing gastric interoceptive attention.

cards.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder.
cards.post: Aim: To address this gap, we conducted a translational study combining clinical assessments in 55 patients with major depressive disorder, 57 BD patients, and 55 healthy controls, alongside sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mouse models. Results: Our findings revealed significantly elevated peripheral creatine concentrations in both BD patients and model mice, which correlated with increased hepatic expression of guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), a rate-limiting enzyme in creatine biosynthesis. Conclusion: Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention.

cards.title: From Rapid Synaptic Events to Lasting Antidepressant States: Convergent and Divergent Mechanisms of Ketamine and Psychedelics.
cards.venue: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
cards.post: Background: Rapid-acting antidepressants have challenged the long-standing view that therapeutic improvement in major depressive disorder requires chronic treatment with monoaminergic agents. Results: We first discuss hippocampal mechanisms underlying ketamine action, which include brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB)-dependent homeostatic potentiation, TrkB cross talk with metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) at CA3→CA1 synapses, extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK)-dual-specificity phosphatase 6 (DUSP6)-mediated extension of synaptic metaplasticity, and BDNF release at mossy fiber synapses and dentate gyrus neuronal maturation. Conclusion: Together, these studies suggest that antidepressant efficacy arises not from a single pathway or brain region but from coordinated, temporally staged plasticity across molecules, synapses, cells, and circuits.

cards.title: EXPRESS: Blood-free full quantification of dynamic TSPO PET imaging with [11C]PBR28.
cards.venue: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
cards.post: Background: Quantitative dynamic PET imaging requires metabolite-corrected arterial input functions, traditionally obtained through invasive arterial blood sampling, limiting broader adoption of quantitative kinetic modelling. Methods: We developed ASTRA, a deep-learning-based framework for arterial input function estimation from dynamic brain TSPO PET. Results: ASTRA-derived quantitative estimates agreed with arterial measurements (VT: CCC=0.658-0.805), with higher uncertainty associated with greater error. In the clinical cohort, ASTRA reproduced SUVR-based group differences using DVR (p<0.001), except in the pituitary gland (p=0.12). Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi-site, non-invasive quantitative TSPO PET.

cards.title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
cards.post: Background: Alpha band (8-13 Hz) electroencephalography (EEG) oscillations are central to cognition, but their generating mechanisms are poorly understood. Methods: Ultra-high-field (UHF, 7T) laminar functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) enables cortical depth resolved brain responses, and, combined with simultaneous EEG, offers new insight into human alpha generation mechanisms. Results: After deveining, the negative alpha-BOLD correlations were significantly weaker in the middle cortical depths than in superficial and deep depths. This depth dependence was absent when modelling the task with a boxcar regressor rather than EEG alpha power, suggesting specificity to spontaneous electrophysiological (alpha) fluctuations. Conclusion: In conclusion, we have established a method to non-invasively interrogate the origins of electrophysiological signals.

cards.title: Probabilistic mapping of brain connections without random sampling
cards.post: Background: For two decades, most tractography has mapped brain connections by sampling millions of pathways probabilistically. Results: We show that it is unnecessary: modeling tractography as an absorbing Markov chain gives the expected result of infinitely many streamlines. This approach is more reliable than streamline-based tractography across test--retest scans. Conclusion: MPAT is available as open-source software at https://github.com/rokemlab/mpat .

cards.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore.
cards.post: Background: After the African origin of Homo sapiens, multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. Methods: In this study, we report on 'Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Results: Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Conclusion: Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

cards.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials.
cards.post: Background: Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. Methods: Here we introduce scale-rich metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving orders-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity. Conclusion: This network-based framework establishes a minimal and universal model for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical behaviour emerges directly from scale diversity, and also opens avenues of enquiry for network science itself.

cards.title: Psilocybin desynchronizes the human brain
cards.post: Background: It remains unclear how human brain network changes relate to subjective and lasting effects of psychedelics. Methods: Here we tracked individual-specific brain changes with longitudinal precision functional mapping (roughly 18 magnetic resonance imaging visits per participant). Results: Performing a perceptual task reduced psilocybin-driven FC changes. Psilocybin caused persistent decrease in FC between the anterior hippocampus and default mode network, lasting for weeks. Conclusion: Persistent reduction of hippocampal-default mode network connectivity may represent a neuroanatomical and mechanistic correlate of the proplasticity and therapeutic effects of psychedelics.
